chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the found object (luqatah). He said: 'It is announced for one year, whether it is little or much.' He said: 'And whatever is less than a dirham is not announced.'

key_terms.الدِّرْهَم: A dirham, a silver coin used as a threshold for value in legal rulings
key_terms.اللُّقَطَة: Found object or lost property picked up from the ground
key_terms.تُعَرَّفُ: It is announced / made known (to the public)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for announcing and keeping found money or items?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the procedural standard for *luqatah* (found property) in Shia jurisprudence, mandating a one-year public announcement period to ensure the owner's right is preserved. The exemption for items valued under a dirham reflects the juristic principle of avoiding undue burden (*ghurm*) for trivial finds, balancing legal rigor with practical ease. This ruling is foundational in the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for distinguishing between significant assets requiring formal custody and minor items where the cost of announcement outweighs the benefit.
